newsitem.title: POLAND: Lithuania, Poland declare mutual support on Europe.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania, Poland declare mutual support on Europe.

text.p: Lithuania's foreign minister Algirdas Saudargas said in Warsaw on Monday his country saw Poland as its key partner in its aspirations to join NATO and the European Union.

"We consider that Poland is the main geo-political, geo-strategic partner in this direction, and this is included in the Lithuanian government's programme," Saudargas, who picked Warsaw for his first visit abroad as foreign minister, said after talks with his Polish counterpart Dariusz Rosati.
Rosati told a joint news conference that Warsaw and Vilnius both saw it as in their interests for the other to enter the two structures.
Poland hoped Lithuania would be among the first countries to be asked to enter talks on joining the European Union, he said.

Poland expects to be among the first former Soviet bloc states to join NATO in 1999, while the former Soviet republic of Lithuania's membership is more remote, partly because of still more strenuous objections to its entry from Moscow.

Rosati said the two countries were creating a joint military battalion, which should become operational in 1998 and would recall past military cooperation between the two nations which were linked in a commonwealth centuries ago.

Poland has expressed concern over published comments by Lithuania's Education Minister, Zigmas Zinkevicius, suggesting Polish-language secondary schools, serving the Polish minority in Lithuania, should teach in Lithuanian.
Saudargas, who spoke in fluent Polish, said this was not his government's policy and Lithuania would uphold obligations under international treaties to uphold the rights of minorities.

The two ministers said they were watching developments in Belarus, where President Alexander Lukashenko has dissolved the former parliament and set up a new one, and would consider joint initiatives of their two or more countries if warranted.
Late last year, the presidents of Poland, Lithuania and Ukraine issued a joint statement expressing concern over the future of democracy in their common neighbour Belarus.
Saudargas, who also held talks with Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Monday, is due to meet President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Tuesday.
